fixes.what: The 1916 occupation of eastern Macedonia by Bulgaria had no month, no page and confidence 1.

fixes.fix: month 8, confidence 2, source Macedonian_front (added to sources) (done).

fixes.what: The end of the Bulgarian occupation was dated 1919 at confidence 1 from the Cliopatria shape.
fixes.why: Macedonian front page: Bulgaria was 'granted the Armistice of Salonica' on 29 September 1918; 'The Macedonian front ended at noon on 30 September 1918'. principality-of-bulgaria dates its occupation_end 1918-9.

fixes.what: Crete is gained twice: from cretan-state in October 1908 (/ledger/15) and again from ottoman-empire on 14 December 1913; the second gain has no mirror (the Ottoman dossier lost Crete to cretan-state in 1900).
fixes.why: Treaty of Bucharest (1913) page: 'Crete was definitively assigned to Greece and was formally taken over on 14 December that year'; cretan-state ends 1908-10 with dissolve into first-hellenic-republic; Cliopatria has Crete Greek from 1908. Flagged by the author as open.
fixes.fix: Keep the 1908 gain (Cliopatria and cretan-state agree) and fold the 14 December 1913 takeover into its note, or turn the 1913 event into a non-territorial note; do not gain the island twice. Non-blocking.

fixes.what: Cliopatria shapes 1822-1865 carry a stray rectangle at 7.52-7.60 E, 49.58-49.65 N (the Palatinate, Germany); no keyframe note or correction mentions it (the 1866 note calls it 'a stray vertex').
fixes.why: Cliopatria geometry: one ring of 5 vertices in every First Hellenic Republic shape from 1822 to 1865, hence the shapes.csv bbox starting at 7.5155 E; it maps to no H3 r5 cell, so it does not reach the grid.
fixes.fix: Add one sentence to the 1822 keyframe note (or notes) naming the stray fragment as a Cliopatria error to drop. Non-blocking.

fixes.fix: verdict adjust, correction the 1913 shape (plus the 1917 Aegean cells) for 1916-1918, with /ledger/27-28 drawing the hatch. Non-blocking.

fixes.fix: correction = the 1920 shape minus admin1 Izmir, Manisa, Aydin, Balikesir, Bursa and Usak (Turkey). Non-blocking.
